### Relief of a burden claimed as deserved

The [permitted-relief study](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PERMITTED-RELIEF-AND-DESERT-INTEGRATION.md) now tests the very adverse episode alleged to be deserved. Wrongdoing, the continuing experience, affected claims and the available relieving transformation are relations within one unfolding history. The comparison grants exact desert and independently warranted permission locally; it does not establish their joint realization in an actual case. Relief reduces the remaining deserved burden, so the alleged loss of fitting desert is retained rather than silently removed.

The affirmative judgment is that this response can be worth choosing for the sufferer's sake before a helping commitment exists. Actual relief supplies a patient-directed point that an empty gesture or suppression of distress reports lacks. This is a defended ethical assessment; neither its permission nor the beneficial effect alone proves it. The [strongest rival](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PERMITTED-RELIEF-AND-DESERT-COUNTERREVIEW.md) preserves the experience while claiming that desert excludes this moral contribution. It remains a substantive challenge, not an established counterexample.

The [primary comparisons](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PERMITTED-RELIEF-AND-DESERT-SOURCES.md) prevent treating an adverse desert ranking as absence of every relief reason. The [affirmative argument](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PERMITTED-RELIEF-AND-DESERT-ARGUMENT.md) also identifies a third possibility: context changes suffering's moral contribution while remission has value. That value still needs a patient-directed ground preceding adopted concern; a virtuous motive or special relationship would not by itself establish the proposed universal minimum. No innocence restriction, additive value formula or new Lean premise is introduced.

A theory allowing punishment, a prohibition on interfering with a sentence, and a reason to impose suffering answer different questions. Permission to cause suffering is not absence of every reason to alleviate it. The minimum's positive account must defend continued favor in the appropriate case; the rival must justify genuine extinction rather than merely a stronger contrary reason. Adding “undeserved” to eligibility would evade the universal claim rather than establish it. This is a focused test of the existing grounding obligation, not an accepted exception or a new completion gate.
